title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the statement of the Deligne–Mumford(–Knudsen) theorem begun on the previous page. Grothendieck writes it 'Mumford–Deligne' and uses 'MD-courbes' for stable ν-pointed curves. The stack \hat M_{g,ν} of stable curves of numerical type (g,ν), with 2g+ν ≥ 3, is a smooth proper algebraic stack over Spec Z. The stack M_{g,ν} of smooth curves is an open substack of it, schematically dense in every fibre; this sentence finishes the theorem.

First consequence. Geometric connectedness of the fibres of M_{g,ν} in every characteristic follows from connectedness in characteristic 0. This is the original Deligne–Mumford argument, run in four steps:
- \hat M_{g,ν} is proper and flat over Z with geometrically connected generic fibre (by transcendental methods, via Teichmüller theory).
- By Zariski's connectedness theorem / Stein factorisation, all geometric fibres of \hat M are connected.
- Smoothness then makes them irreducible.
- Density of M_{g,ν} in each fibre gives irreducibility, hence connectedness, of the fibres of M_{g,ν}.

Second point. Fix a type [G] of 'MD-graph', i.e. the dual graph of a stable curve: vertices with genera, legs carrying the marked points, edges for the nodes, of total numerical type (g,ν). The 'standard curves' of type [G] over any base S are stable curves of type (g,ν). They are obtained by gluing smooth pointed curves along pairs of sections, as in the preceding pages. This gives a canonical morphism (25) M_{[G]} → \hat M_{g,ν}, which Grothendieck says is easily checked to be an immersion. Here M_{[G]} is the stack of curves with dual graph isomorphic to G, essentially the product of the M_{g_v,n_v} modulo Aut(G).

The next page continues the thread:
- For the trivial graph (one vertex of genus g, ν legs, no edges) one recovers the open immersion M_{g,ν} ⊂ \hat M_{g,ν}.
- The M_{[G]} form a finite partition of \hat M_{g,ν} into locally closed substacks: the stratification by dual graphs.
- Closures of strata are unions of strata, which defines a specialisation order on graph types.

The purpose is to set up the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν}: the boundary stratification that later feeds the Teichmüller tower and the discussion of tangential base points and fundamental groupoids.
errors: No mathematical error. One minor imprecision: the immersion statement requires M_{[G]} to be the quotient by Aut(G), equivalently the stack of curves whose dual graph is isomorphic to G. The gluing map from the product of the M_{g_v,n_v} itself is finite onto the closed stratum, not an immersion. The notes appear to intend the quotient version.

ideas.what: Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen compactification: smooth proper stack \hat M_{g,ν} over Z, with M_{g,ν} open and fibrewise dense
ideas.modern_name: moduli stack of stable pointed curves \bar M_{g,n}
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) mentions \hat M_{g,ν} and its structure at infinity

ideas.what: Connectedness of the fibres in characteristic p deduced from characteristic 0 via properness and Zariski connectedness
Locally closed immersions M_{[G]} → \hat M_{g,ν} indexed by stable dual graphs, giving a finite stratification
ideas.modern_name: boundary stratification of \bar M_{g,n} by stable graphs
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford, Knudsen; standard in later work (e.g. Arbarello–Cornalba–Griffiths)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the stratification at infinity

deep.surprise_reason: This is a faithful, expository restatement of well-known Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen results and the standard dual-graph stratification. Nothing here is new.
transcription_corrections: Line 4: the image shows struck-out words; it reads roughly 'en [barré] car., à partir de [barré] connexité en car. 0', i.e. 'en toute car.' with 'toute' deleted, and the connectedness is 'connexité en car. 0'.

'(sur un base quelc. S) sont universelles [?] des MD-courbes relatives' should most likely read '(sur une base quelc. S) sont des MD-courbes relatives de type numérique (g,ν)'. The word 'universelles' looks like a misreading of a crossed-out word followed by 'des'.
Equation numbers: this page's (25) is correct. The next page's '(76)' is probably '(26)'.
